notes: Asserts ready → working → waiting when GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77, launched in plan mode (--plan), emits its ExitPlanMode analogue and blocks on the approval overlay. MARKED known_failing: the spec states the CORRECT arc, which daemon 0.5.9 does not produce. PROBED RED through the production tailer before writing this spec — an open tool.execution_start with toolName=exit_plan_mode gives HasOpenToolCall=true, LastOpenToolNames=[exit_plan_mode], TranscriptPermissionPending=false, and therefore NeedsUserAttention=false, IsAgentDone=false, IsWaitingForUserInput=false, so the classifier's default transcript-activity rule keeps the session in `working` for the whole time the user is blocked. The identical metrics with claudecode's PascalCase `ExitPlanMode` return NeedsUserAttention=true: the entire defect is a missing snake_case entry in isUserBlockingTool (core/domain/session/metrics.go:450) and its documented twin tailer.isUserBlockingToolName — the list already carries vibe's snake_case ask_user_question, so this is the established shape. The approval REQUEST itself is unobservable either way (exit_plan_mode.requested/.completed are emitEphemeral, like user_input.requested and unlike permission.requested), so the tool call is the only trace — but it IS a persisted one, which is why this is bug and not incapable. --allow-all is deliberately kept on so the plan-mode write gate never fires permission.requested: the waiting transition is then attributable to exit_plan_mode alone, not to the 2-19 rule. PRESESSION shape (PROVISIONAL, from the driver + adapter, not a recording): Copilot creates the session-state directory at launch and writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so a transient proc-<PID> row is born before the real session (id = the directory name via sessionIDFromPath) reconciles under a DIFFERENT session_id — every post-birth phase anchors to the REAL session. OBSERVATIONS assert `agent` only, matching 2-19: the run terminates mid-turn in waiting, before any assistant.turn_end / session.usage_checkpoint / session.shutdown, so cost and tokens are legitimately unreliable here. The recipe never answers the overlay, so final state = waiting, mirroring the claudecode and codex siblings.
